Annotation Interface RequiresRecentSignIn

@Target({METHOD,TYPE,ANNOTATION_TYPE}) @Retention(RUNTIME) @Documented public @interface RequiresRecentSignIn
The caller must have signed in recently: within who.security.recent-sign-in (10 minutes by default), or within within(). Use it on actions a stolen session should not be able to take, such as making an API key. 
@PostMapping("/keys")
@RequiresPermission("keys.write")
@RequiresRecentSignIn
public NewKey make(...) { ... }
  • A browser session that signed in too long ago gets 401 ReauthenticationRequiredException: sign the person in again, then retry.
  • A JWT whose auth_time is too long ago gets 401 with the RFC 9470 step-up challenge, InsufficientUserAuthenticationException.
  • A JWT without auth_time, and an API key, get 403 RecentSignInUnavailableException: neither can ever be recent.

On a type it covers every method; it works as a meta-annotation too. It is enforced by who's method security (who.method-security.enabled), after any @PreAuthorize or @RequiresPermission check on the same method. For URL rules, use the RecentSignInAuthorizationManager bean: .access(recentSignIn).
